name: Margaret Hale

biography.childhood: Born and raised in a working-class family in Cleveland, Ohio. Eldest of four siblings. Helped raise her younger brothers after her mother fell ill when Margaret was twelve.
biography.career: Worked for 28 years as an elementary school teacher at Lincoln Elementary, teaching second grade. Retired at 62. Well known for reading aloud to her class every Friday afternoon.
biography.family: Married to Walter Hale for 51 years until his death in 2016. Two children: Susan (b. 1963) and David (b. 1966). Four grandchildren. Susan visits most often.
biography.hobbies: Loved gardening, especially roses. Played piano casually. Enjoyed baking bread on Sunday mornings for the family.

family_members.name: Walter Hale
family_members.notes: Died in 2016. Margaret sometimes asks for him as though he is still alive; this is expected and should not be corrected harshly.

family_members.name: Susan Hale-Porter
family_members.notes: Visits weekly. Margaret often mistakes her for her own sister, Ellen.

family_members.name: David Hale
family_members.notes: Lives out of state, visits less frequently.

family_members.name: Ellen
family_members.notes: Died in 1998. Margaret frequently confuses Susan with Ellen.

biographical_facts.fact: Margaret taught second grade at Lincoln Elementary School for 28 years.
Margaret was married to Walter Hale for 51 years.
Margaret has two children, Susan and David.
Margaret grew up in Cleveland, Ohio.
Margaret loved growing roses in her garden.
Margaret baked bread every Sunday morning.
Margaret's younger sister was named Ellen.

episodic_memories.text: Reading a picture book aloud to a classroom of second graders on a Friday afternoon, the children gathered on a rug.
Standing in the garden in early June, cutting the first roses of the season and bringing them inside in a chipped blue vase.
Walter proposing at the edge of a lake during a summer picnic, nervous and fumbling with the ring box.
Sitting at the kitchen table kneading bread dough on a Sunday morning while the children argued in the next room.
Her mother being too ill to get out of bed, and Margaret making breakfast for her younger brothers before school.
Holding her newborn daughter Susan for the first time in the hospital.
The hospital room where Walter died, the sound of the machines, Susan holding her hand.

sensitive_topics: being asked to recall the current date or year
being told a deceased family member has died
distress_triggers: insisting Walter is deceased when she asks for him
correcting her when she misidentifies a family member
quizzing her on facts, names, or dates
redirection_notes: Responds best to validation-oriented redirection: acknowledging her feelings, gently shifting to a sensory or positive memory (roses, baking, the classroom) rather than correcting factual errors directly.
